## Jira story HMA-401957
Summary: Basic Multi-armed Bandit option for A/B testing
Type: Story | Status: In Development
Components: - | Labels: -
Description / Acceptance criteria:
In addition to existing options in A/B testing for selecting the branch, we will add multi-armed bandit ([https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-armed_bandit|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-armed_bandit|smart-link] ) as a move towards integrating more AI capability, even though we only implement the basic case.

To do this, the below new configuration settings are added to A/B test UI

# Threshold on total presentation of all the branches.
# Minimum percentage (minPer) to be selected for for random selection.

This is how it works

# Initially, the branches are selected randomly based on the initial configured percentage
# When the threshold is reached, the random selection is applied in only minPercentage of the cases; while the branch with the highest acceptance rate is selected for the rest. For example, if minPer=10, random selection is applied in 10% of the getOffers call, and the best performant branch is selected in 90% of the cases.
# The best performant branch is dynamically evaluated, although not necessarily for every getOffers call. The evaluation for best offer should consider the recent data rather than considering the contact & accept counts from the beginning. The logic for “recent data“ is to be decided.

Components InteractDT (Design Time), RTP

1. Overview 
 
A multi-armed bandit (MAB) is a dynamic testing method that continuously shifts traffic toward 
the best-performing variation. Unlike traditional A/B testing, it prioritizes maximizing 
conversions over strict statistical significance. It automatically reduces traffic to poor 
performers, saving revenue while the test is running. 
 
MAB algorithms balance two goals simultaneously:  
• Exploration: Randomly testing all variations to gather data and find the best one. 
• Exploitation: Directing most of your traffic to the variation with the highest proven 
success rate. 
 
 
1.1 Background 
The existing A/B Testing feature in Unica Interact supports three selection modes: 
 
Mode Value Description 
UseDefault 0 When threshold reached, use 
the configured default branch 
 
Classification: Internal 
Mode Value Description 
AutoSelect 1 System automatically selects 
the best-performing branch 
UseBase 2 Use the base/control branch 
 
These modes provide static or semi-static branch selection. To move towards AI-driven 
decisioning, we introduce a Multi-Armed Bandit approach that dynamically balances 
exploration (trying all branches) and exploitation (favouring the best performer). 
1.2 Objective 
Implement a basic Multi-Armed Bandit (Epsilon-Greedy variant) selection mode that: 
 
- Explores all branches initially using configured percentages 
- After a presentation threshold is reached, shifts to exploiting the best-performing branch 
while maintaining a configurable exploration rate 
- Dynamically re-evaluates the best branch based on recent acceptance rate data 
 
 
2. Functional Requirements 
2.1 New Selection Mode 
Add MultiArmedBandit(3) to the ABTestSelectionMode enum.

2.3 Behavior 
�Phase 1 (Exploration): totalPresentations < threshold 
  → Select branch randomly based on configured sample percentages 
 
Phase 2 (Exploit + Explore): totalPresentations >= threshold 
  → With probability (minPercent / 100): select randomly per configured percentages 
  → With probability (1 – (minPercent / 100)): select the branch with highest recent 
acceptance rate 
�2.4 Example 
- 3 branches configured with percentages 40%, 35%, 25% 
- Threshold = 500, MinPercent = 10 
- For first 500 presentations:  
- random selection (40/35/25 distribution) 
- After 500 total presentations: 
- 10% of getOffers calls → random selection (40/35/25 distribution) 
- 90% of getOffers calls → best-performing branch selected
